# Constellations — provenance report

<!-- Generated from authored/constellations.json by scripts/authored_decks.py. Do not edit: change the dossier and rebuild. -->

**Deck:** [`decks/constellations.ttl`](../decks/constellations.ttl) · **Cards:** 88 · **Licence:** [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) · **Compiled by:** Anton Wiklund · **Created:** 2026-10-04

All 88 constellations recognised by the International Astronomical Union, in 88 cards studied both ways. Front: the constellation's official Latin name; back: its English and Swedish names, with the IAU abbreviation in a note. Names from the IAU's constellation table and Wikidata, checked against NASA, Wikipedia and Nationalencyklopedin.

## Licensing

The deck is licensed CC BY 4.0 because its list of constellations, their Latin names and abbreviations and, above all, their English names (the IAU table's “English Name” column, popular names that are not mere literal translations) are taken from the IAU's page “The Constellations”, whose web texts the IAU releases under CC BY 4.0; the IAU is credited as a source in the deck (prov:wasDerivedFrom, with title, creator and licence) and in this report, and the changes made to its English names (leading “the” dropped, two spellings corrected, eight figure names used instead of descriptions) are listed in the method. Using the IAU page as a content source was a deliberate choice: the CC0 alternatives cover the list and abbreviations (Wikidata; NASA's public-domain table) but not a consistent set of English names (Wikidata's English aliases are incomplete and inconsistent), and CC BY 4.0 lets anyone reuse the deck, commercially too, with attribution. The IAU’s credit conditions are met: the IAU is named, unaltered, in the deck description, in the deck metadata and in the notes that quote its popular names, and nothing in the deck states or implies IAU endorsement. The Swedish names come from Wikidata (CC0), which places no conditions. The NASA page (a US government work), the Swedish Wikipedia article and the English Wikipedia articles (CC BY-SA 4.0), and Nationalencyklopedin (all rights reserved; free quotation only for non-commercial use) were used only to verify facts: no wording, list or selection was taken from them, so their licences put no conditions on the deck. The notes are the authoring agent's own wording.

## Method

1. Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.
2. The list of constellations, their Latin names, abbreviations and English names come from the IAU's page “The Constellations”. Its old address (https://www.iau.org/public/themes/constellations/) returns 404 since the IAU's site was redesigned, and the new iau.org has no constellation page linked from its home page. The page was found in the IAU's own web archive at https://iauarchive.eso.org/public/themes/constellations/ (the reference used by the English Wikipedia article) and downloaded with curl on 2026-10-04; an Internet Archive copy of the old iau.org page from 2023-12-30 was also downloaded and has the identical table. The table under “Charts and tables” was parsed with a short Python script (parse_iau.py, reproduced verbatim under Queries; HTML tags stripped, the download links dropped, the remaining cells read in groups of six: name, pronunciation, abbreviation, English name, genitive, genitive pronunciation). It gives exactly 88 rows.
3. Each card's front is the IAU name exactly as the table spells it (e.g. “Boötes” with its diaeresis), tagged as Latin. All 88 are tagged Latin by convention, Dorado included: the IAU names serve as the constellations’ scientific Latin names and are declined as Latin (the IAU table gives the genitive “Doradus”), although “dorado” itself is a Spanish word, as the Dorado card’s note says. The back's English text is the table's “English Name” (described on the page as “the popular name in English”) without its leading “the” (“the Great Bear” → “Great Bear”), with three kinds of exception: (a) Coma Berenices: the table reads “the Bernice's Hair”; the deck spells it “Berenice’s Hair”, as the Latin name itself (Berenices) and Wikipedia's Meaning column (“Berenice's hair”) do. (b) Pyxis: the table reads “the Mariner Compass”; the deck uses the usual English form “Mariner’s Compass” (Wikipedia's Meaning column: “mariner's compass”). (c) Eight constellations named after a figure — Andromeda, Cassiopeia, Cepheus, Eridanus, Hercules, Orion, Pegasus and Perseus — have the figure's own name as their English name, which is what English uses for them; the IAU table gives descriptions for seven of them (“the Chained Maiden”, “the Seated Queen”, “the King”, “the River”, “the Hunter”, “the Winged Horse”, “the Hero”; for Hercules it reads “the Hercules”), and those descriptions are quoted in the card's note instead. Using them as answers would have made the reversed cards ambiguous (“Hero” fits Hercules as well as Perseus) and would not translate the Swedish name on the same card (Cassiopeja, Orion, …).
4. The Swedish names are the Swedish labels (rdfs:label @sv) of the Wikidata items. The items were found with one SPARQL query on https://query.wikidata.org/sparql (listed under Queries) that matches each IAU name against English labels of items that are instances of constellation (Q8928) or a subclass of it and have a short name (P1813); it returned exactly one item for each of the 88 names, and for every item the short name equals the IAU abbreviation. The English and Swedish aliases of the 88 items were fetched with a second query, so that a Wikidata check could also be added where an alias is exactly the card's English text. A first exploratory query (instances of Q8928 only) returned 97 items: it missed Aries and Cancer, which Wikidata types only as zodiac constellation (Q4193029), and included historical or non-IAU constellations (e.g. Sciurus Volans, Marmor Sculptile, Pomum Imperiale); it was used only to see how the data is modelled.
5. Swedish cross-check: every Swedish label was compared with the table “Tabell över stjärnbilderna” in the Swedish Wikipedia article “Stjärnbild” (wikitext fetched with https://sv.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=Stj%C3%A4rnbild&prop=wikitext|revid&format=json&formatversion=2, revision 59706601), parsed with a Python script. That script was not kept; the parsing rules are reproduced by parse_svwiki.py (under Queries), written during review round 2, which gives exactly the same 87 rows from the same saved wikitext (the rowspan rows of Giraffen/Camelopardalis are skipped and that row added by hand, as in the original). All 88 Swedish names and all 88 abbreviations agree. The names follow Swedish convention: definite form of a common noun with a lower-case second word (“Stora björnen”, “Södra korset”), and the Swedish forms of personal names (“Cassiopeja”, “Herkules”).
6. English cross-check: every English name and abbreviation was compared with the “List” table of the English Wikipedia article “IAU designated constellations” (parsed with parse_enwiki.py, under Queries; wikitext fetched with https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=IAU_designated_constellations&prop=wikitext|revid&format=json&formatversion=2, revision 1375575250). The Meaning column agrees with the IAU's English name for most constellations; where it differs (listed in quality control, round 0) the deck keeps the IAU's name, since the IAU is the authority for the list and the Wikipedia column gives a literal meaning rather than a popular name.
7. Abbreviation and list cross-check: the NASA/GSFC page “Three-Letter Constellation Abbreviations” was downloaded with curl and its table parsed; it lists the same 88 constellations with the same abbreviations (in capitals). NASA and Wikidata spell Boötes without the diaeresis in some places (NASA “Bootes”, Wikidata's Latin label “Bootes”); the deck follows the IAU spelling, which is also Wikidata's English label.
8. The generator script make_dossier.py (reproduced verbatim under Queries, together with wd_fetch.py and wd_aliases.py, which ran the two Wikidata queries; the raw downloads were kept in a temporary working directory of the authoring agent that is not published) asserts for every card that the IAU abbreviation equals the Wikidata short name, the Swedish Wikipedia abbreviation and the NASA abbreviation, and that the Wikidata Swedish label equals the Swedish Wikipedia name; it then writes each card with its evidence from all five sources. Each card’s note gives the IAU abbreviation and, in the authoring agent’s own words, an explanation where the English and Swedish names clearly differ in meaning (Boötes, Capricornus, Cetus, Corvus, Hydra, Hydrus, Horologium, Pictor, Reticulum, Taurus, Telescopium), where the IAU’s popular name is not used as the answer, or where the name itself needs a word (Dorado); notes on Swedish variants (Cassiopeia, Eridanus, Vela) were added in review round 1. Smaller nuances (e.g. Vela “Sails” / Seglet, singular) get no note.
9. Review rounds 1–3 were applied to the dossier by apply_rounds.py and round 4 by apply_round4.py (both reproduced verbatim under Queries). apply_rounds.py reads the saved downloads and review fetches (NE openings, English Wikipedia leads) and edits the dossier that make_dossier.py wrote; replay.py (also under Queries) re-ran it on a saved copy of that pre-review dossier and found the result identical to the published dossier before round 4.
10. Swedish names, independent check (added in review rounds 1–2): for every card, Nationalencyklopedin’s article was fetched by the script ne_fetch.py (under Queries) from https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/lång/<Swedish name, lower case, spaces as hyphens>, falling back to <…>-(stjärnbild), and the opening sentence (the free part of the article) kept as evidence. NE gives the card’s Swedish name as the headword for 85 of the 88 cards. The three others: Cassiopeja (NE’s headword is “Cassiopeia”, with “Cassiopeja” as a variant), Eridanus (NE’s main article is “Floden Eridanus”; “Eridanus” is a cross-reference to it) and Seglet (NE calls it “Seglen”, plural). These cards keep the Wikidata and Swedish Wikipedia name, which the builder checks, and give NE’s form in the note.
11. English names, second check (added in review round 3): where English Wikipedia’s list renders the IAU’s English name differently, and for the meanings given in the notes, the lead sections of the English Wikipedia articles on those constellations were fetched with the MediaWiki API (under Queries) and the sentence that confirms the name or meaning is quoted in the card’s evidence. The Swedish names of species used in the notes (korp, stenbock, guldmakrill) were looked up as Wikidata labels and are checked at every build.
12. Every card has machine checks against Wikidata, run by the builder: the English label equals the IAU Latin name, the Swedish label equals the card's Swedish name, and the short name (P1813) equals the IAU abbreviation; where Wikidata has the card's English text as an English alias, that alias is checked too.
13. Study direction is bidirectional: the builder confirms that every English and every Swedish back text is unique in the deck, so the reversed cards (English or Swedish name → Latin name) each have one answer. For 11 constellations the English name is the Latin name (Andromeda, Cassiopeia, Cepheus, Eridanus, Hercules, Lynx, Orion, Pegasus, Perseus, Phoenix, Sculptor), and for six of them the Swedish name is too (Andromeda, Cepheus, Eridanus, Orion, Pegasus, Perseus), so the reversed card gives its answer away; that is inherent to the subject and was accepted.

## Selection

The deck has exactly the 88 constellations in the IAU's table, which are the constellations the IAU recognises (the list agreed in 1922, with boundaries adopted in 1928 and published in 1930); nothing was added and nothing left out. Historical constellations that the IAU does not recognise (Wikidata types some of them as constellations, e.g. Sciurus Volans and Marmor Sculptile) are excluded. Asterisms such as the Big Dipper/Karlavagnen are not constellations and are excluded. Genitive forms, pronunciations, boundaries and star names are left out to keep each card to one fact: the constellation's names.

**parse_iau.py: parse the IAU table into 88 rows (authoring)** (The Constellations)

```
import re, html, json
D = '/tmp/claude-1000/-home-antwika-dev-github-antwika-solid-memo/29afcb49-8c27-4a6e-be7b-e04afdd93785/scratchpad/constellations/'
s = open(D + 'iauarchive-constellations.html', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
s = re.sub(r'(?s)<script.*?</script>', '', s)
t = re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', '\n', s)
t = html.unescape(t)
lines = [l.strip() for l in t.split('\n') if l.strip()]
i = lines.index('Downloads')
cur = []
for l in lines[i + 1:]:
    if l == 'Charts Text Legend':
        break
    if (l.startswith('Constellation charts') or l.startswith('Constellation boundary') or l in ('GIF', 'PDF', 'TIF', 'TXT')
            or re.match(r'^\(?\d+ ?KB\)?$', l) or l.startswith('(')):
        continue
    cur.append(l)
print(len(cur))
recs = []
for k in range(0, len(cur), 6):
    g = cur[k:k + 6]
    assert re.fullmatch(r'[A-Z][A-Za-z]{2}', g[2]), g
    recs.append({'name': g[0], 'abbr': g[2], 'english': g[3], 'genitive': g[4]})
print(len(recs))
json.dump(recs, open(D + 'iauarchive-table.json', 'w'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
for r in recs:
    print(r['name'], '|', r['abbr'], '|', r['english'], '|', r['genitive'])
```

**parse_enwiki.py: parse the “List” table of “IAU designated constellations” (authoring)** (IAU designated constellations)

```
import json, re
D = '/tmp/claude-1000/-home-antwika-dev-github-antwika-solid-memo/29afcb49-8c27-4a6e-be7b-e04afdd93785/scratchpad/constellations/'
w = json.load(open(D + 'enwiki-iau-designated.json'))['parse']['wikitext']
i = w.find('=== List ===')
t = w[i:]
t = t[:t.find('\n|}')]
rows = t.split('\n|-')[2:]


def clean(c):
    c = re.sub(r'<ref[^>]*/>', '', c)
    c = re.sub(r'(?s)<ref.*?</ref>', '', c)
    c = re.sub(r'\{\{efn[^}]*\}\}', '', c)
    c = re.sub(r'\{\{IPAc-en[^}]*\}\}', '', c)
    c = re.sub(r'\{\{br\}\}', ' ', c)
    c = re.sub(r'data-sort-value="[^"]*"\s*\|', '', c)
    c = re.sub(r'\[\[(?:[^|\]]*\|)?([^\]]+)\]\]', r'\1', c)
    c = c.replace("''", '')
    return c.strip()


out = {}
for r in rows:
    r = r.strip().lstrip('|').strip()
    first = r.split('\n')[0]
    cells = [clean(c) for c in first.split('||')]
    name = cells[0].strip()
    meaning = cells[8] if len(cells) > 8 else '?'
    out[name] = {'iau': cells[1], 'meaning': meaning}
json.dump(out, open(D + 'enwiki-table.json', 'w'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
iau = json.load(open(D + 'iauarchive-table.json'))
print(len(out))
for r in iau:
    m = out.get(r['name']) or out.get(r['name'].replace('ö', 'o'))
    print(r['name'], '|', r['abbr'], '|', r['english'], '||', m)
```

**wd_fetch.py: run the query for the 88 items (authoring)** (Wikidata)

```
import json, urllib.parse, urllib.request
D = '/tmp/claude-1000/-home-antwika-dev-github-antwika-solid-memo/29afcb49-8c27-4a6e-be7b-e04afdd93785/scratchpad/constellations/'
recs = json.load(open(D + 'iau-table.json'))
values = " ".join(f'"{r["name"]}"@en' for r in recs)
query = f"""SELECT ?item ?en ?sv ?la ?short (GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ?type; separator=" ") AS ?types) WHERE {{
  VALUES ?en {{ {values} }}
  ?item rdfs:label ?en ;
        wdt:P31 ?type ;
        wdt:P1813 ?short .
  ?type wdt:P279* wd:Q8928 .
  OPTIONAL {{ ?item rdfs:label ?sv FILTER(LANG(?sv) = "sv") }}
  OPTIONAL {{ ?item rdfs:label ?la FILTER(LANG(?la) = "la") }}
}} GROUP BY ?item ?en ?sv ?la ?short ORDER BY ?en"""
open(D + 'wd-query.rq', 'w').write(query)
data = urllib.parse.urlencode({"query": query, "format": "json"}).encode()
req = urllib.request.Request("https://query.wikidata.org/sparql", data=data, headers={
    "User-Agent": "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)",
    "Accept": "application/sparql-results+json"})
res = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120))
json.dump(res, open(D + 'wd-88.json', 'w'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
rows = res["results"]["bindings"]
print(len(rows))
by = {}
for r in rows:
    g = lambda k: r.get(k, {}).get("value", "")
    by.setdefault(g("en"), []).append((g("item").rsplit("/", 1)[1], g("sv"), g("la"), g("short"), g("types")))
for r in recs:
    print(r["name"], by.get(r["name"]))
```

**parse_svwiki.py: parse “Tabell över stjärnbilderna” (written in review round 2 to reproduce the unsaved original parse; same output)** (Stjärnbild)

```
import json, re
D = '/tmp/claude-1000/-home-antwika-dev-github-antwika-solid-memo/29afcb49-8c27-4a6e-be7b-e04afdd93785/scratchpad/constellations/'

        continue

    out[cells[1]] = [sv, cells[3]]
print(len(out))
old = json.load(open(D + 'svwiki-table.json'))
print('identical to svwiki-table.json:', out == old)
for k in sorted(set(out) ^ set(old)):
    print('differs:', k, out.get(k), old.get(k))

**make_dossier.py: assemble the dossier from the saved downloads (authoring; rounds 1–3 were applied afterwards by apply_rounds.py)** (The Constellations)

```
"""Assemble authored/constellations.json from the saved raw responses in this directory."""
import json, re, unicodedata

D = '/tmp/claude-1000/-home-antwika-dev-github-antwika-solid-memo/29afcb49-8c27-4a6e-be7b-e04afdd93785/scratchpad/constellations/'
OUT = '/home/antwika/dev/github/antwika/solid-memo/.claude/worktrees/authored-decks/packages/deck-library/authored/constellations.json'
TODAY = '2026-10-04'
SV_REV = json.load(open(D + 'svwiki-stjarnbild.json'))['parse']['revid']
EN_REV = json.load(open(D + 'enwiki-iau-designated.json'))['parse']['revid']

iau = json.load(open(D + 'iauarchive-table.json'))
wd_rows = json.load(open(D + 'wd-88.json'))['results']['bindings']
wd = {}
for r in wd_rows:
    g = lambda k: r.get(k, {}).get('value', '')
    wd[g('en')] = {'qid': g('item').rsplit('/', 1)[1], 'sv': g('sv'), 'la': g('la'), 'short': g('short')}
aliases = {}
for r in json.load(open(D + 'wd-aliases.json'))['results']['bindings']:
    q = r['item']['value'].rsplit('/', 1)[1]
    aliases.setdefault((q, r['text']['xml:lang']), set()).add(r['text']['value'])
sv_table = {k: v for k, v in json.load(open(D + 'svwiki-table.json')).items()}
sv_table['Camelopardalis'] = ['Giraffen', 'Cam']
sv_table['Crux'] = sv_table.pop('Crux (Australis)')
sv_table['Boötes'] = sv_table.pop('Bootes')
sv_table_latin = {'Crux': 'Crux (Australis)', 'Boötes': 'Bootes', 'Camelopardalis': 'Camelopardalis'}
en_table = {}
for k, v in json.load(open(D + 'enwiki-table.json')).items():
    en_table[re.sub(r'\s*\{\{.*?\}\}\s*', '', k).strip()] = v
nasa_html = open(D + 'nasa-constel_names.html', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
nasa_text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', nasa_html))
nasa = dict((m.group(2).strip(), m.group(1)) for m in re.finditer(r'\b([A-Z]{3}) ([A-Z][a-z]+(?: [A-Z][a-z]+)?) ', nasa_text))

# The IAU's popular English name is used without its leading "the", except:
PROPER = {  # constellations named after a figure: the English name is the figure's name
    'Andromeda': 'Andromeda', 'Cassiopeia': 'Cassiopeia', 'Cepheus': 'Cepheus', 'Eridanus': 'Eridanus',
    'Hercules': 'Hercules', 'Orion': 'Orion', 'Pegasus': 'Pegasus', 'Perseus': 'Perseus',
}
CORRECTED = {'Coma Berenices': "Berenice's Hair", 'Pyxis': "Mariner's Compass"}
EXTRA_NOTE = {
    'Cetus': ('The Swedish name means “the whale”.', 'Det engelska namnet betyder ”havsodjuret”.'),
    'Pictor': ('The Swedish name means “the painter”.', 'Det engelska namnet betyder ”målarens staffli”.'),
    'Hydrus': ('The Swedish name means “the lesser water snake”.', 'Det engelska namnet betyder ”den manliga vattenormen”.'),
}


def slug(s):
    s = unicodedata.normalize('NFKD', s).encode('ascii', 'ignore').decode()
    return re.sub(r'[^a-z0-9]+', '-', s.lower()).strip('-')


cards = []
findings = []
for r in iau:
    name, abbr, iau_en = r['name'], r['abbr'], r['english']
    w = wd[name]
    assert w['short'] == abbr, (name, w['short'], abbr)
    sv_name, sv_abbr = sv_table[name]
    assert sv_name == w['sv'], (name, sv_name, w['sv'])
    assert sv_abbr == abbr, (name, sv_abbr)
    assert nasa[name.replace('ö', 'o')] == abbr.upper(), name
    popular = iau_en[4:] if iau_en.startswith('the ') else iau_en
    en = PROPER.get(name) or CORRECTED.get(name) or popular
    note_en = f'IAU abbreviation: {abbr}.'
    note_sv = f'IAU-förkortning: {abbr}.'
    if name in PROPER and name != 'Hercules':
        note_en += f' The IAU’s popular English name: “{iau_en}”.'
        note_sv += f' IAU:s populärnamn på engelska: ”{iau_en}”.'
    if name in EXTRA_NOTE:
        note_en += ' ' + EXTRA_NOTE[name][0]
        note_sv += ' ' + EXTRA_NOTE[name][1]
    cid = slug(name)
    ent = en_table[name.replace('ö', 'o')] if name not in en_table else en_table[name]
    evidence = [
        {'source': 'iau', 'locator': f'The Constellations, “Charts and tables”, row {name}',
         'says': f'Name “{name}”; Abbr. “{abbr}”; English Name “{iau_en}”; genitive “{r["genitive"]}”.',
         'retrieved': TODAY},
        {'source': 'wikidata', 'locator': f'https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/{w["qid"]}',
         'says': f'English label “{name}”, Swedish label “{w["sv"]}”, Latin label “{w["la"]}”, short name (P1813) “{abbr}”.',
         'retrieved': TODAY},
        {'source': 'nasa', 'locator': 'Three-Letter Constellation Abbreviations table',
         'says': f'{abbr.upper()} — {name.replace("ö", "o")}', 'retrieved': TODAY},
        {'source': 'svwiki', 'locator': f'Stjärnbild, “Tabell över stjärnbilderna” (revision {SV_REV})',
         'says': f'Namn på stjärnbild “{sv_name}”, Latinskt namn “{sv_table_latin.get(name, name)}”, Förk. “{abbr}”.',
         'retrieved': TODAY},
        {'source': 'enwiki', 'locator': f'IAU designated constellations, “List” table (revision {EN_REV})',
         'says': f'IAU abbreviation “{ent["iau"]}”; Meaning “{ent["meaning"]}”.', 'retrieved': TODAY},
    ]
    checks = [
        {'qid': w['qid'], 'label': 'en', 'equals': name},
        {'qid': w['qid'], 'label': 'sv', 'equals': w['sv']},
        {'qid': w['qid'], 'property': 'P1813', 'expect': abbr},
    ]
    if en != name and en in aliases.get((w['qid'], 'en'), set()):
        checks.append({'qid': w['qid'], 'label': 'en', 'equals': en})
    cards.append({
        'id': cid,
        'front': {'la': name},
        'back': {'en': en, 'sv': w['sv']},
        'backNote': {'en': note_en, 'sv': note_sv},
        'evidence': evidence,
        'checks': checks,
    })
    if w['la'] != name and name != 'Boötes':  # Boötes has its own finding in dossier-meta.json
        findings.append({'card': cid, 'issue': f'Wikidata’s Latin (la) label is “{w["la"]}”, not the IAU spelling “{name}”.',
                         'resolution': 'The front uses the IAU spelling, which is also Wikidata’s English label (checked); the Latin label is not used or checked.',
                         'outcome': 'no change needed'})

meta = json.load(open(D + 'dossier-meta.json'))
meta['qualityControl']['rounds'][0]['findings'] = meta['qualityControl']['rounds'][0]['findings'] + findings
for q in meta['queries']:
    if q['query'].startswith('@file:'):
        q['query'] = open(D + q['query'][6:]).read().strip()
meta['cards'] = cards
json.dump(meta, open(OUT, 'w'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
open(OUT, 'a').write('\n')
print(len(cards), 'cards;', sum(len(c['checks']) for c in cards), 'checks;', len(findings), 'la findings')
for c in cards:
    print(c['id'], '|', c['back']['en'], '|', c['back']['sv'], '|', len(c['checks']))
```

**ne_fetch.py: fetch NE’s article for every Swedish name (review rounds 1–2)** (Nationalencyklopedin (uppslagsverk, långa artiklar))

```
"""Fetch Nationalencyklopedin's article for each card's Swedish name and keep the article's opening text."""
import json, re, html, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request
R = '/tmp/claude-1000/-home-antwika-dev-github-antwika-solid-memo/29afcb49-8c27-4a6e-be7b-e04afdd93785/scratchpad/constellations/round1/'
DOSSIER = '/home/antwika/dev/github/antwika/solid-memo/.claude/worktrees/authored-decks/packages/deck-library/authored/constellations.json'
UA = 'solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)'
BASE = 'https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/l%C3%A5ng/'


def fetch(slug):
    url = BASE + urllib.parse.quote(slug)
    try:
        t = urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers={'User-Agent': UA}), timeout=30).read().decode('utf-8', 'replace')
    except Exception as e:
        return url, None
    t = re.sub(r'(?s)<(script|style)[^>]*>.*?</\1>', ' ', t)
    txt = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', html.unescape(re.sub(r'<[^>]+>', ' ', t)))
    m = re.search(r'Skriv ut (.{0,400})', txt)
    return url, (m.group(1) if m else None)


d = json.load(open(DOSSIER))
out = {}
slugs = [(c['id'], c['back']['sv']) for c in d['cards']] + [('extra', 'Floden Eridanus'), ('extra', 'Cassiopeia'), ('extra', 'Seglet (stjärnbild)')]
for cid, sv in slugs:
    base = sv.lower().replace(' ', '-')
    got = None
    for s in [base, base + '-(stjärnbild)']:
        url, lead = fetch(s)
        time.sleep(0.5)
        if lead and 'stjärnbild' in lead:
            got = {'url': url, 'lead': lead}
            break
    out[cid + ':' + sv] = got
    print(cid, sv, '=>', got and got['lead'][:160], flush=True)
json.dump(out, open(R + 'ne.json', 'w'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
```

**apply_rounds.py: apply review rounds 1–3 to the dossier** (The Constellations)

```
"""Apply the review rounds 1-3 to authored/constellations.json (run once)."""
import json, re, urllib.parse

R = '/tmp/claude-1000/-home-antwika-dev-github-antwika-solid-memo/29afcb49-8c27-4a6e-be7b-e04afdd93785/scratchpad/constellations/round1/'
S = '/tmp/claude-1000/-home-antwika-dev-github-antwika-solid-memo/29afcb49-8c27-4a6e-be7b-e04afdd93785/scratchpad/constellations/'
OUT = '/home/antwika/dev/github/antwika/solid-memo/.claude/worktrees/authored-decks/packages/deck-library/authored/constellations.json'
TODAY = '2026-10-04'
d = json.load(open(OUT))
assert len(d['qualityControl']['rounds']) == 1, 'already applied'
cards = {c['id']: c for c in d['cards']}
src = d['sources']

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- sources
src['iau']['licenseEvidence'] += (

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- NE evidence on every card
ne = json.load(open(R + 'ne.json'))
ne_seglen = {'url': 'https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/l%C3%A5ng/seglen',
             'lead': 'Seglen, Veʹla , stjärnbild på södra stjärnhimlen, ej synlig från Sverige. Seglen är en del av den större antika konstellationen Skeppet Argo .'}


def first_sentence(lead):
    lead = lead.split(' Information om artikeln')[0].strip()
    m = re.search(r'\. (?=[A-ZÅÄÖ])', lead)
    s = lead[:m.start() + 1] if m else lead
    if len(s) > 240:
        s = s[:240].rsplit(' ', 1)[0] + ' …'
    return s


def ne_ev(entry, note=''):
    loc = urllib.parse.unquote(entry['url']) + ', opening sentence (the rest of the article is behind a paywall)'
    return {'source': 'ne', 'locator': loc, 'says': f'“{first_sentence(entry["lead"])}”' + note, 'retrieved': TODAY}


for c in d['cards']:
    key = f"{c['id']}:{c['back']['sv']}"
    if c['id'] == 'vela':
        c['evidence'].append(ne_ev(ne_seglen, ' No NE article “Seglet” was found (also tried “seglet-(stjärnbild)”);'
                                              ' NE’s article “Vela” reads “Veʹla, det latinska namnet på stjärnbilden Seglen .”'))
    elif c['id'] == 'cassiopeia':
        c['evidence'].append(ne_ev(ne['extra:Cassiopeia'], ' (No NE article at the slug “cassiopeja”; the headword is “Cassiopeia”.)'))
    elif c['id'] == 'eridanus':
        c['evidence'].append(ne_ev(ne[key]))
        c['evidence'].append(ne_ev(ne['extra:Floden Eridanus']))
    else:
        assert ne[key], key
        c['evidence'].append(ne_ev(ne[key]))

    'circinus': ('Circinus', 'Its name is Latin for compass, referring to the drafting tool used for drawing circles (it should not be confused with Pyxis, a constellation that represents a mariner\'s compass which points north).'),
    'crater': ('Crater (constellation)', 'One of the 48 constellations listed by the second-century astronomer Ptolemy, it depicts a cup that has been associated with the god Apollo and is perched on the back of Hydra the water snake.'),

    'capricornus': ('Capricornus', 'Its name is Latin for "horned goat" or "goat horn" or "having horns like a goat\'s", and it is commonly represented in the form of a sea goat: a mythical creature that is half goat, half fish.'),
    'corvus': ('Corvus (constellation)', 'Its name means "raven" in Latin.'),

    'reticulum': ('Reticulum', 'Its name is Latin for a small net, or reticle—a net of crosshairs at the focus of a telescope eyepiece that is used to measure star positions.'),

    'horologium': ('Horologium (constellation)', 'It was first described by the French astronomer Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille in 1756 and visualized by him as a clock with a pendulum and a second hand.'),

for cid, (title, sentence) in EN_ART.items():
    rev, ex = leads[title]
    assert ' '.join(sentence.split()) in ' '.join(ex.split()), (cid, sentence)
    cards[cid]['evidence'].append({'source': 'enwiki-articles', 'locator': f'“{title}”, lead section (revision {rev})',
                                   'says': f'“{sentence}”', 'retrieved': TODAY})
cm_sentence = "The star marked the Great Dog's mouth on Bayer's star atlas."

cards['canis-major']['evidence'].append({

    'says': f'“{cm_sentence}” (of Sirius); the lead reads “Its name is Latin for \"greater dog\" in contrast to Canis Minor, the \"lesser dog\"”.',
    'retrieved': TODAY})

    cards[cid]['checks'].append({'qid': qid, 'label': 'sv', 'equals': {'Q25357': 'korp', 'Q168327': 'stenbock', 'Q14443': 'Guldmakrill'}[qid]})

b = json.load(open(CUR))
def diff(x, y, p=''):
    if type(x) != type(y):
        print('TYPE', p); return
    if isinstance(x, dict):
        for k in set(x) | set(y):
            if k not in x or k not in y: print('KEY', p + '/' + str(k), k in x, k in y)
            else: diff(x[k], y[k], p + '/' + str(k))
    elif isinstance(x, list):
        if len(x) != len(y): print('LEN', p, len(x), len(y))
        for i, (u, v) in enumerate(zip(x, y)): diff(u, v, p + '/' + str(i))
    elif x != y:
        print('VAL', p, repr(x)[:200], '|', repr(y)[:200])
diff(a, b)
print('done')

## Quality control

5 rounds, 40 findings: 26 fixed, 0 rejected after checking, 14 needing no change. Every card's Wikidata checks (270 in all) are re-run against live Wikidata by `scripts/authored_decks.py check` before every build.

### Round 0: Sources and machine checks: every card against the IAU table, Wikidata, NASA and both Wikipedias; the builder's Wikidata checks. (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — authoring agent, machine checks · **Scope:** All 88 cards.

The IAU table, Wikidata (short name P1813), the Swedish Wikipedia table and the NASA table agree on all 88 constellations and all 88 abbreviations; Wikidata's Swedish labels agree with the Swedish Wikipedia table for all 88. Every card has 3 or 4 Wikidata checks (English label = IAU name, Swedish label, P1813 abbreviation, and the English alias where one exactly matches); all pass at build time. The English names were compared with English Wikipedia's Meaning column; the differences are listed below and resolved in favour of the IAU, except two misspellings in the IAU table. Wikidata's Latin labels use classical spellings for three items; they are not used. Limitation: Wikidata's Swedish labels and the Swedish Wikipedia table are maintained by overlapping communities, so they are not fully independent; no third Swedish list (e.g. Nationalencyklopedin, behind a paywall) was consulted.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| coma-berenices | The IAU table's English name reads “the Bernice's Hair”: an extra article and a misspelling of Berenice (the Latin genitive is Berenices; Wikipedia's Meaning: “Berenice's hair”). | The card reads “Berenice's Hair”. | fixed |
| pyxis | The IAU table's English name reads “the Mariner Compass”; the usual English form is “mariner's compass” (Wikipedia's Meaning column). | The card reads “Mariner's Compass”. | fixed |
| hercules | The IAU table's English name reads “the Hercules”. | The card reads “Hercules”, the English name (also Wikidata's English label). | fixed |
| perseus | The IAU's popular English names for the seven other constellations named after a figure (Andromeda “the Chained Maiden”, Cassiopeia “the Seated Queen”, Cepheus “the King”, Eridanus “the River”, Orion “the Hunter”, Pegasus “the Winged Horse”, Perseus “the Hero”) are descriptions, not names; “Hero” would also fit Hercules when the card is reversed, and none of them translates the Swedish name on the same card. | These cards give the figure's name in English (Andromeda, Cassiopeia, Cepheus, Eridanus, Orion, Pegasus, Perseus) and quote the IAU's popular name in the note. | fixed |
| dorado | IAU: “the Swordfish”; English Wikipedia's Meaning: “mahi-mahi (dolphinfish)”. | Kept “Swordfish”: it is the IAU's popular English name, and the Swedish name Svärdfisken (Wikidata, Swedish Wikipedia) means the same. | no change needed |
| cetus | IAU: “the Sea Monster”; Swedish: Valfisken (the whale). English Wikipedia's Meaning: “sea monster (later interpreted as a whale)”. | Kept both names; the note explains what each means. | no change needed |
| pictor | IAU: “the Painter's Easel”; Swedish: Målaren (the painter). English Wikipedia's Meaning: “painter (originally 'painter's easel')”. | Kept both names; the note explains what each means. | no change needed |
| hydrus | IAU: “the Male Water Snake” (and Hydra “the Female Water Snake”); Swedish Lilla vattenormen (the lesser water snake); English Wikipedia's Meaning: “lesser water snake”. | Kept the IAU's English name; the note gives the meaning of the Swedish name. | no change needed |
| norma | IAU: “the Carpenter's Square”; English Wikipedia's Meaning: “carpenter's level”. | Kept the IAU's name, which also matches the Swedish Vinkelhaken (a try square). | no change needed |
| caelum | IAU: “the Engraving Tool”; Wikidata alias “the Chisel”; English Wikipedia's Meaning: “chisel or engraving tool”. | Kept the IAU's name. | no change needed |
| circinus | IAU: “the Drawing Compass”; English Wikipedia's Meaning: “compasses”; Wikidata alias “the Compass”. | Kept the IAU's name, which also keeps it distinct from Pyxis (Mariner's Compass) when reversed. | no change needed |
| puppis | IAU: “the Stern”; English Wikipedia's Meaning: “poop deck”. | Kept the IAU's name, which matches the Swedish Akterskeppet. | no change needed |
| equuleus | Smaller wording differences between the IAU's English name and English Wikipedia's Meaning column: Equuleus “Little Horse”/“pony”, Libra “Scales”/“balance”, Vulpecula “Fox”/“little fox”, Crater “Cup”/“krater (bowl for mixing wine)”, Crux “Southern Cross”/“cross”, Horologium “Clock”/“pendulum clock”, Ursa Minor “Little Bear”/“lesser bear”, Canis Major “Great Dog”/“greater dog”, Hydra “Female Water Snake”/“Hydra (mythological creature)”, Sculptor “Sculptor”/“sculptor (originally 'sculptor's tools')”. | Kept the IAU's popular English names on all these cards; the Wikipedia column gives literal or original meanings, and none of the differences makes a card wrong. | no change needed |
| bootes | NASA, Wikidata's Latin label and the Swedish Wikipedia table spell the name “Bootes”; the IAU table and Wikidata's English label spell it “Boötes”. | The front uses the IAU spelling “Boötes”, checked against Wikidata's English label. | no change needed |
| canis-major | Wikidata’s Latin (la) label is “Canis Maior”, not the IAU spelling “Canis Major”. | The front uses the IAU spelling, which is also Wikidata’s English label (checked); the Latin label is not used or checked. | no change needed |
| ursa-major | Wikidata’s Latin (la) label is “Ursa Maior”, not the IAU spelling “Ursa Major”. | The front uses the IAU spelling, which is also Wikidata’s English label (checked); the Latin label is not used or checked. | no change needed |

### Round 1: Factual accuracy (2026-10-04)

**Reviewer:** Claude (AI) — independent Factual accuracy reviewer · **Scope:** All 88 cards: Latin names, abbreviations and English names against a fresh parse of the IAU table, Wikidata labels and P1813 live, Swedish names against Nationalencyklopedin.

The reviewer found no wrong card: the IAU table matches every Latin name, abbreviation and English name apart from the documented changes, all Wikidata checks pass, and NE confirms the Swedish name of 86 cards (Seglet unconfirmed). One warning (Eridanus: NE’s main Swedish name is “Floden Eridanus”) and five suggestions. The authoring agent re-fetched NE for every card and confirmed the reviewer’s quotes; it also found what the reviewer could not: NE calls Vela “Seglen”, not “Seglet”. All findings were applied except a description change for the trivial reversed cards, which is documented in the method instead.

| Card | Issue | Resolution | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| eridanus | NE’s main Swedish name is “Floden Eridanus”; its entry “Eridanus” is a cross-reference (“Eriʹdanus, det latinska namnet på stjärnbilden Floden Eridanus.”). The card’s Swedish sources (Wikidata, Swedish Wikipedia) come from overlapping communities. | Verified on ne.se. Kept “Eridanus” (Wikidata label, Swedish Wikipedia title, both checked); added “Kallas även Floden Eridanus (Nationalencyklopedin).” / “Also called Floden Eridanus in Swedish (Nationalencyklopedin).” and both NE entries as evidence. | fixed |
| cassiopeia | NE’s headword is “Cassiopeia”, with “Cassiopeja” as a variant; the method did not say so. | Verified on ne.se (“Cassiopeia [-pɛ i ʹa] , Cassiopeja (latin Cassiopeia …) , stjärnbild på norra stjärnhimlen”). Kept “Cassiopeja” (Wikidata, checked; Swedish Wikipedia); added “Skrivs även Cassiopeia (Nationalencyklopedins uppslagsord).” / “Also spelt Cassiopeia in Swedish (Nationalencyklopedin’s headword).”, NE evidence, and a method step. | fixed |
| capricornus | English “Sea Goat” and Swedish Stenbocken (the ibex) differ in meaning but have no note, unlike Cetus, Pictor and Hydrus. | Added “The Swedish name means “the ibex”.” / “Det engelska namnet betyder ”havsgeten”.” Evidence: Wikidata Q168327 (Capra ibex) Swedish label “stenbock” (checked at build) and the English Wikipedia article “Capricornus” (“commonly represented in the form of a sea goat”). | fixed |
